title: At the Store
subtitle: Emma needs milk, bread and coffee — and the line is long.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about shopping and money: prices, paying, and the words American stores use.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: After work I go to the store. We need milk, bread, and coffee for the shop at home.
The store is near my apartment, so I walk. It is cheap, and it is open until ten.
I take a basket. The milk is two dollars. The bread is three. The coffee is expensive — nine dollars — but it is good coffee, and Jack drinks a lot of it.
I look for apples too, but today they are not fresh. I don't buy them.
At the front there is a long line. I wait for ten minutes. A woman in front of me has two kids, and they are tired and loud.
“Fourteen dollars,” the man says. I pay with a card. He gives me a bag.

exercises.title: Shopping Words
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with one word.

items.prompt: This store is not expensive. It is ___.
items.explanation: Cheap is the opposite of expensive.

items.prompt: I can't find the bread. I ___ ___ it for five minutes.
items.explanation: To look for something is to try to find it.

items.prompt: There are ten people in the ___. I have to wait.
items.explanation: In American English, people waiting one behind the other are in a line.

items.prompt: These apples are from this morning. They are ___.
items.explanation: Fresh means new and good to eat.

items.prompt: I don't have money with me, so I ___ with a card.
items.explanation: To pay is to give money for something.
